en.title: Number of Index Pairs Whose Price Sum Is Divisible by the Discount Number
en.description:
Count the index pairs i<j such that prices[i]+prices[j] is divisible by x. Items have their own identities, so repeated prices can form several pairs, and an item cannot be paired with itself.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and editorial; additions for bounds missing from the sources and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The first line contains n x and the second line contains n prices. The original bounds are 1≤n≤100000, 1≤x≤2×10^9, prices[i]≥1. Only the superscript 9 of the original upper bound on prices survives and its base is missing, so this site explicitly adds price≤10^9 and does not claim this restores the original upper bound.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are 3; 3; and 0, checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: While scanning, first add the frequency of the complementary remainder among earlier items, then increment the count of the current remainder.
